stops.name: Dubai Museum
stops.en: A must-see for anyone interested in the social history of the Emirate (and indeed the country). Located in and under al-Fahidi fort. The fort itself has a few examples of the traditional reed houses and other artifacts, but isn't much to look at. The more interesting parts are the modern galleries beneath the fort, showcasing Dubai's history using the latest technology and culminating in a reconst

stops.name: Dubai Frame
stops.en: Two towers of 150 m height connected by a 100-m² bridge, the Dubai Frame has a museum and gallery where you can see the growth of Dubai from a simple fishing village to the ultra-modern city it is today with the use of photos and advanced technology. After visiting the museum, you take the elevator to the bridge to get a view of the city.

stops.name: Museum of the Future
stops.en: Branded as a "technology museum" many visitors consider it more of an expensive art exhibition. The building is outstanding though and looks particularly impressive in the dark.

stops.name: Emirates Towers
stops.en: The Emirates Towers complex contains the Emirates Office Tower and Jumeirah Emirates Towers Hotel. The two towers, which rise to 355 m (1,165 ft) and 309 m (1,014 ft), respectively, stand as the 23rd and 47th tallest buildings in the world. The two towers are connected by a 9,000 m² (96,875 ft²) two-storey retail complex known as "The Boulevard". The Emirates Towers complex is located on the Sheik

stops.name: Jumeirah Mosque
stops.en: The largest mosque in the city, and a wonderful example of Islamic architecture. It was built in the medieval Fatimid tradition with the interior decorated with elaborate Arabic calligraphy. It is one of few mosques in the city open for visits by non-Muslims; the Sheikh Mohammed Centre for Cultural Understanding conducts special tours for non-Muslims to help promote understanding of Islam. Guided

stops.name: Grand Mosque
stops.en: Its large minaret is the imposing feature of this large mosque. It is popular for being quite close to a Hindu temple and one can see followers of both Islam and Hinduism gathering at the same place for prayers.

stops.name: Al Bastakiya
stops.en: One of the last remaining pockets of Old Dubai, home to many reconstructed buildings in the traditional style. While information on the structures is slim here (see the museum in preference), the atmosphere is very evocative and there are plenty of delightful art galleries and cafes to explore.

stops.name: Burj Khalifa
stops.en: At 828 m and 160 floors this is the world's tallest structure by a long shot, over 300 m taller than the previous contender in Taipei. The observation deck at the 124th floor is the second highest in the world after the Shanghai World Financial centre. Dominating the Dubai skyline, the tower houses a hotel and a Las Vegas-inspired fountain system. The visitors' entrance is at the lower ground floo

stops.name: The Dubai Fountain
stops.en: At 270m (900 ft) in length and sporting a jet that shoots water up to 150m (500 ft), it is the world's largest dancing fountain and one with a very enticing display - a definite must-see. It's most easily accessed via the Dubai Mall. There are private entranceways from the Burj Khalifa if you're staying there.

stops.name: Maktoum Bin Rashid Al Maktoum Stadium
stops.local: ملعب مكتوم بن راشد آل مكتوم

stops.name: Deira Clocktower
stops.en: A landmark of Deira and important as a monument built before the independence of UAE.

stops.name: Iranian Mosque, Bur Dubai
stops.en: A very colourful and attractive tiled mosque; quite a contrast to the other much more plainly decorated mosques. Can be viewed from a carparking area off the north (creek) side of the street.

stops.name: Safa Park
stops.en: A beautiful planned park and one of the oldest parks in Dubai. It is a favourite for sports enthusiasts, and many visitors enjoy playing tennis, volleyball, and soccer. Children love playing games in the video arcade, or riding the Ferris wheel and bumper cars. The park even has a maze to wander through. Barbeques and picnic areas are available for those who want to make a day of it. It has lakes

stops.name: Zabeel Park
stops.en: The best and most popular park of town, it gives a remarkable glimpse of the desert and hot Dubai.

stops.name: Dubai Dolphinarium
stops.en: The only indoor dolphinarium in the Middle East offers live shows of dolphins and seals. Swim with Dolphins is possible.

stops.name: Etihad Museum
stops.en: Museum about the construction of the Union of the Emirates, after the withdrawal of British forces. Open in 2017, it features exhibits about the seven fathers, and the constitution. The Union House, where the treaty was signed, can be visited as well as the Guest Palace. It also hosts temporary exhibitions (e.g., philatelic in May 2017).

stops.name: Majlis Ghorfat Umm Al Sheif
stops.en: A restored traditional Emirati-style two story building used as a summer residence by Sheikh Rashid bin Saeed Al Maktoum, one of the founders of UAE, and father of the present ruler of Dubai.

stops.name: Creek Park
stops.en: A great place to hang out in the evening when the park is visited by people of different nationalities, all looking for calm place to enjoy the time. It has all the facilities of a modern park and is one of the best parks in Dubai. The cable car is closed.

stops.name: Al Ahmadiya School and Heritage House
stops.en: Built in 1912, Al Ahmadiya School was Dubai's first school and has now been nicely restored. It would be a stretch to call the exhibits of old reed pens and diplomas fascinating, but they've tried pretty hard, and if nothing else, the air-con and clean toilets may come in handy. The attached heritage house is a traditional Emirati-style home built in the 1890s.

stops.name: Dhow Wharfage
stops.en: The dhows ply the Arabian Sea and the Indian Ocean, transporting goods between south and south-west Asia and east Africa.

stops.name: Mamzar Park
stops.en: You can swim at Al Mamzar Beach or stroll in the park. Though less popular than other Dubai parks, it has its share of Dubai's greenery. Monday & Wednesday for women only.

stops.name: Women's Museum
stops.en: Highlight the contribution of women to UAE's economy, culture and politic for the independence in the 1960s and since. Life of great women and daily life of Emirati people. An exhibit is also dedicated to the famous Emirati female poet Ousha bint Khalifa Suwidi.

stops.name: Gold Price Checking - Dubai Souq
stops.en: Before purchasing gold in Dubai’s famous Gold Souk, it's always best to check the current live gold prices. Gold prices fluctuate daily due to global market trends. Visit [GoldRateUAE](https://goldrateuae.ae/) to get the latest price updates. Prices here are available for various gold types including 22K, 24K, and 18K gold.

stops.name: Sheikh Mohammed Centre for Cultural Understanding
stops.en: If you want to learn and understand the customs and traditions of UAE, this is the best place to go. The Centre hosts cultural meals for between 70 and 95 AED, with discussion of UAE culture, customs and religion. They run walking tours through the Bastakiya district for 60 minutes (35 AED) and 90 minutes (55 AED), starting at either 9 or 10:30AM daily except Friday.

stops.name: Heritage Village
stops.en: Home to the open museums of the Heritage and Diving Villages, and the houses of the late Sheikhs Saeed Al-Maktoum and Juma Al-Maktoum.

stops.name: Sheikh Obaid bin Thani House
stops.en: a historic building home to royal family members built in 1916 and now converted into a museum. It provides good glimpse to old infrastructure of Dubai.

stops.name: Saeed Al Maktoum House
stops.en: Another very historic building built in 1894 now converted into a museum and contains artefacts and images of the old town of Dubai. It was the residence of the Saeed bin Maktoum bin Hasher Al Maktoum, the former ruler of Dubai.

stops.name: Crossroad of Civilization Museum
stops.en: Museum includes a lot of artefacts and old books, including a Gutenberg Bible and a curtain of the door of Kaaba from 1543 AD.

stops.name: Old Weapons Museum
stops.en: Large collection of swords, daggers, riffles, from several centuries.

stops.name: Dubai Aquarium and Underwater Zoo
stops.en: Giant aquarium, long and high. The visit includes a crossing inside the walk-through water tunnel, behind the scenes, and several other experiences. The Underwater Zoo has 140 fish species, desert animals, penguins and also hosts "King Krok". Animal feeding hours are indicated in the zoo, and it's also possible to participate during feeding.

stops.name: Jumeirah Fishing Harbor
stops.en: A quiet place with some nice restaurants.

stops.name: Sky Views Dubai
stops.en: This hotel building offers beautiful views toward Burj Khalifa from its 53rd floor observation deck. There is a 25-m glass floor walk and a ride on a glass slide included. For another dirham a walk along the edge of this building floor can be booked.

stops.name: Imagine
stops.en: Plays two different big water, fire and light shows: Stardancer and A Child's Dream. Have several world records.

stops.name: Rugby Park
stops.en: A 5,000-seat field hockey stadium. The stadium will provide a base to the UAE Hockey Committee and the WorldHockey Academy. The Hockey Stadium is situated at the Dubai Sports City Academy's Campus and provides world-class facilities for international athletes and local enthusiasts. The World Hockey Academy is the first facility of its kind anywhere in the world. Through a partnership between Dubai

eats.note: An Indian restaurant

eats.name: Al Bait ALqadeem Restaurant and Cafe
eats.note: A traditional restaurant

eats.name: Al-Karmel Somali Restaurant
eats.note: East African cuisine

eats.name: Africana Home Restaurant Nakheel Deira Park
Al Dawaar Revolving Restaurant
eats.note: Serving an assortment of cuisines, the highlight of this beautiful restaurant is that it revolves, giving a nice tour of the city.

eats.name: Kiku
eats.note: Japanese cuisine. Very high quality and very popular.

eats.name: Legends Steakhouse
eats.note: Part of the Creek Golf Clubhouse. The waterfront restaurant right on Dubai Creek is very popular with residents.

eats.name: Floating Restaurants
eats.note: Tens of dhows propose a diner during a 2-hour cruise on the creek.

eats.name: JW's Steakhouse
eats.note: This is the Marriott's signature restaurant. Very popular with Dubai residents.

eats.name: Filli Cafeteria
eats.note: Probably the most popular tea spots in town, especially Filli, who serves over 4,000 cups a day. Try the zaffrani chai (milk tea with saffron) or the doodh kadak (strong milk tea).

eats.name: The Edge Pool & Bar
eats.note: Small bar but wonderful views especially at sunset.

eats.name: X Club
eats.note: Russia-themed bar.

eats.name: Gharana
eats.note: Gharana an Indian Restaurant in Holiday Inn Dubai – Al Barsha hotel brings you flavors of various spices and herbs with live entertainment.

eats.name: Basta Art Cafe
eats.note: Set in a lovely garden courtyard in a restored house. Great place to take a breather with a cold drink and write some postcards. The sandwiches-and-salads menu is aimed squarely at tourists, but if yo

eats.name: Gazebo
eats.note: Very nice and warm welcome given by the waiters. Food as good too. Not so expensive when compared to the quality of food.

eats.name: Ravi Restaurant
eats.note: A Pakistani restaurant that provides cheap Pakistani & Indian food. Good for anyone with a spicy tooth.

eats.name: Student Biryani
eats.note: A Pakistani restaurant serving the country's most popular biryani.

eats.name: Local House
eats.note: Emirati cuisine featuring camel meats and camel milkshakes in a traditional Dubai house.

eats.name: Al Haj Bundu Khan
eats.note: Indian and Pakistani food.

eats.name: Pars Iranian Kitchen
eats.note: This is an open air Iranian restaurant where one can sit in traditional machans (large bed-like seating) and enjoy a fine Iranian meal. The speciality is the mixed grill which is served with live coal

eats.name: Wafi Gourmet
eats.note: Excellent Lebanese cuisine and ambience. In the cooler months the outdoor verandah is a pleasure. No alcohol served.

eats.name: Yakitori House
eats.note: Japanese cuisine, very popular with the Japanese expat community.

eats.name: Asha's
eats.note: Indian cuisine. Run by Asha Bosle. Good food but a little expensive

eats.name: Manhattan Grill
eats.note: Fine dining restaurant with New York-inspired cuisine, specialising in steak. A suitable venue for romantic dinners and family gatherings.

eats.name: Barrels Pub
eats.note: It is a bar is a clean, quiet and bright venue with large variates of snacks options. Every wall is mounted with screen playing number of sports games. The interiors looks good with polished timber ta

eats.name: Bollywood Café
eats.note: Excellent DJ, Live music and Indian food. It is a Bollywood-themed glamorous bar and nightlife with elegant to casual laid backs and pleasant musical twists, mostly Indian music.

eats.name: Chill Rooftop Lounge
eats.note: Dance floor with excellent DJ. It is an expansive rooftop venue painted in pink surrounded with fake grass. An outdoor seating place with good food.

eats.name: Marine's Club
eats.note: A lively bar and nightclub with 80s music most of the time. It is a budget friendly venue with great service and superb bouncers.

eats.name: 800 Pizza
eats.note: Traditional & authentic Italian pizza baked in wood fired Italian stone oven, thin & crispy crust.

eats.name: More Cafe
eats.note: Serves breakfast, lunch and light continental and oriental meals. Good service and big portions.

eats.name: Noodle House
eats.note: Asian food.

eats.name: Chill Out
eats.note: Have a delicious contemporary European food in ice lounge at a chilling temperature of . It is first of its kind in the Middle East. From tables to even crockery in which food is served, all made of i

eats.name: Chimes
eats.note: Thai, Singaporean, Malaysian and Indonesian themed food, and the popular house speciality must be the pepper or chili crab. You can eat at the restaurant or order home delivery to most areas of new Du

eats.name: Jedoudna Restaurant
eats.note: A family-run Lebanese restaurant. With outdoor seating and separate shisha area.

eats.name: Karam Beirut
eats.note: Excellent Lebanese food.

eats.name: Lal Qila Dubai
eats.note: Pakistani cuisine.

eats.name: London Fish & Chips
eats.note: Fish, chips, sharky meals, traditional battered, baked potatoes, sandwiches, salads and soups

eats.name: Toscana
eats.note: Italian.

eats.name: Al Fresco
eats.note: Specialized in Italian food with cosy outdoor seating. Business lunch, Family friendly place. Smoking and alcohol is permitted. Try the garlic bruschetta with traditional tomato, the leafy green salad

eats.name: Al Mahara
eats.note: Part of the Burj Al Arab hotel, and as you would expect is also very high quality, especially seafood.

eats.name: At.mosphere
eats.note: Exclusive fine dining restaurant on Level 122 of Burj Khalifa.

eats.name: The Gem Garden
eats.note: Continental restaurant.

eats.name: Margaux
eats.note: European, steak and continental cuisine. Pleasing and stunning ambiance with variations and one could enjoy the views of Burj Khalifa and the fountain shows.

eats.name: Options, by Sanjeev Kapoor
eats.note: Run by famed Indian TV chef Sanjeev Kapoor. Drinks served. Reservations recommended especially on Friday nights.

eats.name: The Royal Budha
eats.note: Authentic Thai restaurant.

eats.name: Shang Palace
eats.note: Good Chinese food. No smoking

eats.name: Al Nafoorah
eats.note: Arabic, Lebanese and Middle Eastern cuisines. Outdoor seating with perfect sense of fine dining accompanied with comfortable, Arabian-style terrace. Smoking and alcohol is permitted.

Jumeirah Beach Hotel Complex. Open air bar with great views of the Burj hotel and the Jumeirah beach hotel all helped by a cool breeze from the ocean. Various DJs but think Ibiza lounge bar and you wi

eats.name: Buddha Bar
eats.note: Branch of the international Asian-themed bar/restaurant. Full of crowds.

eats.name: Barasti
eats.note: Built in three levels (each playing its own music), with lounging areas on the beach, lots of young and foreign people come here during the weekend. Very popular with expats.

eats.name: Nasimi Beach
eats.note: Great bar/club on the beach in the Palm Jumeirah.

eats.name: Long's Bar
eats.note: The longest bar in the UAE, typical English style with live football, similar to a UK Wetherspoons. Great music and DJs plus food and friendly atmosphere.

eats.name: Left Bank
eats.note: O the waterfront in one of the most tranquil areas of Dubai. A great food menu leads on to some excellent cocktails and music inside.

eats.name: Observatory
eats.note: Bar and restaurant with great view across Palm Jumeirah (on a clear day!) Popular happy hour with the after work crowd on Thursday from 18:00-20:00.

eats.name: Skyview Bar
eats.note: Live local and international bands, reservations are a must.

eats.name: Vu's Bar
eats.note: Try the 51st Floor house cocktail, it's so deliciously strong, also there's a staggering 200 cocktails to choose from.

eats.name: Zero Gravity
eats.note: Beach club, a nice place for partying.

eats.name: VIP Room
eats.note: It is a lounge-like lively space that offers mid-range to high-price drinks. The huge multi-color circular space is cornered by large LCD screens and exclusive tables and the scantily clad podium danc

eats.name: The Act
eats.note: This venue is full of dance artists, mischievous performances, women performing unusual stunts and on-stage antics. It is a place where you will forget that you are in Dubai. The drinks are good and a

eats.name: The Cigar Bar
eats.note: Specialized in true cigar aficionado, cognacs and whiskies. Smoking is permitted. Dresscode is smart casuals. It is a traditional venue with modern rich dark enveloping and mahogany lined interior fur

eats.name: Zinc
eats.note: It is the city’s most popular nightclubs with girls night out, dance floor and variety of DJ sets. This place is always over crowded and the drinks are budget friendly.

eats.name: Jebel Ali Club
eats.note: A good restaurant with relaxing pub, pools, darts, swimming pool and steam rooms. The drink and food is budget friendly.

eats.name: The Kebab Shop
eats.note: Good budget friendly food specialized in British, Pakistani, Indian and Turkish food

eats.name: Kcal Healthy Fast Food
eats.note: Healthy fast food and great dining experience.

eats.name: Chicken Tikka Inn
eats.note: Awesome place for great Indian food.

eats.name: La Fontana
eats.note: Mediterranean cuisine, generous breakfast buffet, international dishes and a variety of themed dinner buffets, either indoors or on the large outdoor terrace.

eats.name: Mushref Bar
eats.note: Shaded by palm trees with numerous pool bars, entertainment zones and sunbeds.

eats.name: Palmito Pool Bar
eats.note: Swim-up pool bar serving good drinks and refreshments.

eats.name: Sunset Lounge
eats.note: Great Beverages.

eats.name: Diablo Nightclub Dubai
eats.note: It is a Moroccan Themed lounge that serves cocktails, shisha, teas and coffees.

eats.name: Al Mallah
eats.note: Amazing food. It is popular for casual dining, juices, sandwiches and fast food. A good place to visit along with family and friends.

eats.name: Sidra
eats.note: Specialized in Arabic, Lebanese and Middle Eastern Foods. This spacious alfresco area is bigger than other restaurants, full of shrubs and bushes with two distinct large indoor spaces - smokers and no
